html:
The Belarusian protests of 2020 and 2021 were mass demonstrations against Alexander Lukashenko after the presidential election of 9 August 2020, which he claimed to have won with about 80 percent of the vote.

The opposition candidate Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, who stood in place of her jailed husband, was widely seen as the real winner. Hundreds of thousands marched in Minsk on Sundays under the white red white flag of the 1918 republic. Police beat and detained tens of thousands, and nearly all opposition leaders were jailed or forced abroad. By 2021 the movement had been crushed. The crisis pushed Belarus into dependence on Russia and cut it off from the European Union.
sum: The Belarusian protests of 2020 and 2021 were mass demonstrations against Alexander Lukashenko after the presidential election of 9 August 2020, which he claimed to have won with about 80 percent of the vote.
